title: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 1-52 — Three years
N.C. Gen. Stat. § 25-2-725 — Statute of limitations in contracts for sale
content:
N.C. Gen. Stat. § 25-2-725

(1) An action for breach of any contract for sale must be commenced within four years after the cause of action has accrued. By the original agreement the parties may reduce the period of limitation to not less than one year but may not extend it.

title: Bland v. Norfolk Southern Ry. Co., 355 N.C. 599 (2002)
content:
Bland v. Norfolk Southern Ry. Co., 355 N.C. 599 (2002).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Court of North Carolina addressed contributory negligence and held that a plaintiff's contributory negligence, if established, bars recovery unless the defendant's conduct rises to the level of gross negligence, willful or wanton conduct, or intentional wrong.

opinionParts.content: Contributory negligence bars recovery unless the defendant's conduct is gross negligence, willful or wanton, or intentional.
